judgement_on_run_delegation.verdict_on_delegation: ACCEPTABLE. The handler is delegated, not replaced: the accepted function is reached through acceptedRun and the accepted arguments still produce the accepted answer, which is measured rather than asserted, and the direction that would break it is caught (R2-M11).
judgement_on_run_delegation.residual_risk_i_did_not_execute: looksLikeAcceptedRun treats a run invocation with no positional prompt as the accepted cascade, so `researchos run --output jsonl` (contract syntax minus the prompt) starts the Job Object cascade in the current directory instead of reporting a usage error. I deliberately did not run that: it creates a job object and spawns a worker in the shared working tree while another card is executing. The measurement that would settle it without that risk is a row that drives `run --output jsonl` with no prompt and requires exit 2 MISSING_PROMPT.

problems.what: the settled model switch cannot complete in the product because its envelope never carries the writer epoch. apps/cli/cli_v2.go sets env.WriterEpoch only for session.attach and for methods in v2WriteMethods; host.configure is in neither, so a switch that passes the revision check, both settled refusals and the base-url/credential check is sent as {method: host.configure, payload:{... model_id ...}} with writer_epoch absent. internal/domain/client_protocol.go:149-156 refuses that shape for any host.configure naming a model or provider. Measured: 5 of 5 host.configure envelopes I captured were refused by domain.DecodeEnvelope with MODEL_CHANGE_WITHOUT_EPOCH, and against a real apps/control host the command exited 1. The card's evidence cannot see this because its fixture answers COMPLETED to any POST /v2/command without decoding the envelope: adding host.configure to v2WriteMethods, which is the fix, leaves all 89 rows green (R2-M3). Two claims sit in front of that measurement: the comment at apps/cli/cli_contract.go:469-471 says 'The epoch travels in the envelope', and claim_corrections_round1.json's first correction claims 'a completing positive control'.
measured_by: execution/v2.4/receipts/W05/W05-03/reviewer_captured_envelopes_round2.json (host.configure: writer_epoch absent, expected_revision absent, model_id present)
R2-M3 in execution/v2.4/receipts/W05/W05-03/mutation_selfcheck_verifier_round2.json (the fix survives the check)
problems.would_resolve_it: three things, all small. (1) Put the epoch on the wire: add host.configure to the branch that sets env.ExpectedRevision/env.WriterEpoch, and keep the local refusal for the case where none is known. (2) Make the card's host see envelopes the way the resume row already does: assert on the captured envelope that writer_epoch and expected_revision are present for host.configure (W0503-RESUME-SENDS-SESSION-ATTACH already does exactly this for session.attach), or better have the probe host call domain.DecodeEnvelope and answer the refusal it is given, so a wire-invalid envelope cannot be graded as a completion. (3) Correct the two sentences: the cli_contract.go comment and claim_corrections_round1.json correction 1's 'completing positive control'.

problems.what: the contract gives status two operations, session.get and host.status, and only the second is ever exercised. Every status call in the check runs against a config with no session_id, and the row requires hasOp(record,'session.get','SKIPPED'), so the passing state of the card's own evidence is the state where the first operation is not sent. R2-M1 made that leg permanently skipped and all 89 stayed green.
measured_by: reviewer_verb_probe_round2.json (status with a session sends both legs, so the implementation is right and only the evidence is missing)
problems.would_resolve_it: add one status call with --session sess-... and require hasMethod(methods,'session.get') plus a COMPLETED leg, the way the resume row requires its attach envelope.

problems.what: two of the five protocol statuses are mapped to success without any assertion. The fixture never answers IN_PROGRESS or ACKNOWLEDGED; against my server, status with IN_PROGRESS exits 0 and its top-level record says status COMPLETED while the per-leg rows honestly say IN_PROGRESS. The card's action names the exit-code semantics as well as the codes, and an execution report that says COMPLETED for work the host said is still running is the claim the card's own rule forbids.
measured_by: R2-M2 (changing the mapping turns nothing red)
problems.would_resolve_it: grade the five statuses separately with named rows (a not-yet-finished command should report its own status and a code the contract names), or state in the receipt that ACKNOWLEDGED and IN_PROGRESS are treated as reported results at exit 0 and assert that choice.

problems.what: the method column of the command table is copied into commands and help but no row compares it with the envelopes actually recorded, so a row can claim an operation the code never sends (R2-M4 survived). The live instance of that is doctor: contracts/product.contract.json declares local_operations [host.status] for doctor, and the delivered doctor issues GET /healthz and never a protocol command (measured healthz_requests=1, methods=[]). The table hides this by giving doctor an empty method field, so the self-report and the contract disagree silently.
problems.would_resolve_it: compare each row's method column against the probe host's recorded methods for that verb, and either send host.status from doctor or record the deviation as a contract-erratum obligation the way the exit-code change was recorded in doctor_exit_code_correction.json.

problems.what: the proven_by closure is a liveness test, not a relevance test. tableRowsProven asks only whether each named id appears in the ids this run emitted, so pointing a row's proven_by at W0503-CLI-BUILDS and W0503-HEAD-RECORDED satisfies it while proving nothing about init (R2-M5 survived). The mechanism does answer the attack round 1 measured, and it fails closed when a probe disappears (R2-M6, R2-M7), but the deliverable's word 'check' still means 'a row with this name ran'.
measured_by: R2-M5 survived, R2-M6 and R2-M7 caught in mutation_selfcheck_verifier_round2.json
problems.would_resolve_it: bind a probe id to the command it drives: have each v2 row record the verb it invoked and assert that the row named in proven_by was produced by a phase that ran that verb, which is what the SKIPPED/hasMethod rows already do implicitly.

problems.what: the card's evidence is not reliably reproducible on this host. Of 24 executions I ran, 18 gave the identical 89-assertion PASS and 6 FAILED with red rows only in the probe-host phase, every failure detail a transport error against the check process's own 127.0.0.1 listener; the failing row set moved between attempts (20 rows, 16, 22, 19, 1, 2). The check already has the right instrument for this - interrupt130 records not_verified when the platform refuses to deliver a signal - but the probe phase turns a lost connection into a product failure, so a re-run of this card, or of W05-99 later, can read FAIL against unchanged code.
measured_by: runs 1 and 5 of my five standalone runs, and the M9 repeat log
problems.would_resolve_it: detect the transport signature in v2VerbPhase (dial error or deadline exceeded in the record's reason) and turn it into skip('W0503-...','fixture host unreachable: ...') rather than a red row, then re-run the phase once before reporting; the card's stability claim should then state the observed rate rather than 'no row needed a retry'.

problems.what: W05-03's green set depends on a file outside this card's write scope that another card is actively rewriting. W0503-CLI-TABLE-AND-DESKTOP-V2-AGREE reads apps/desktop/main/lib/v2.js. That file is not in git at the HEAD this card was parked at (git cat-file -e 41f3cb96:apps/desktop/main/lib/v2.js -> 'exists on disk, but not in that commit'), so the 89-id PASS is not reproducible from the card's own commit; it was first committed by W13-02 during this review and changed three times while I worked, which is why the digest recorded in remediation_round1.json (f85fcc8d...) no longer matches the file on disk (5745e2c5...). I verified the row itself still holds at 7883e368 by replicating desktopAgrees against the current file: 23 lines with { payload: ', all 23 quoted method names present, payload names equal to the CLI table.
measured_by: git cat-file / git ls-files on apps/desktop/main/lib/v2.js at 41f3cb96 and 7883e368
the digest recomputation in methods step 7
my replicated desktopAgrees check plus clean PASS runs at the new HEAD
problems.would_resolve_it: state the dependency in scope_and_path_notes terms and make it safe: either move the desktop table comparison into a card that owns both copies, or have the row read the published schema as the single authority and treat v2.js as a cross-check that skips (not_verified) when the file is absent, so this card's PASS never depends on a file it does not own.

problems.what: the false attribution round 1 named is still compiled into the binary. apps/cli/main.go:106-108 answers every unregistered verb with 'X is registered to a later card; no silent success'. The card's own table comment (cli_contract.go:73) says the honest owner is not 'a later card', and claim_corrections_round1.json correction 4 retracts that wording for chat. Measured: researchos totally-unknown and researchos chat both print it. Nothing in the accepted harness forces it: the W05-02 pin requires only exit 3 plus the string NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and the W05-02 help pin requires only task/NOT_IMPLEMENTED/chat on stdout.
problems.would_resolve_it: replace the sentence with the machine-readable reason the card already uses (NOT_BOUND_TO_A_CARD plus the owner field from the table) and let the existing W0503-UNKNOWN-VERB and W0503-CHAT rows grade the change; the accepted pins keep passing because they do not name the sentence.

problems.what: a source comment written by the remediation is ahead of the remediation's own behaviour. apps/cli/main.go:89-92 says exit 4 'is left as delivered rather than silently renumbered' and that 'the receipt records the deviation with the row that measures it (W0503-DOCTOR-DOWN-EXIT-4)'. The same file exits 1, doctor_exit_code_correction.json records the change as intentional, and W0503-DOCTOR-DOWN-EXIT-4 is not among the 89 emitted ids (only DOCTOR-DOWN-EXIT-1 is). The stale name also survives in mutation_selfcheck_round4/5.json and in mut_w0503_round4/5.py expected lists, which round 7's note explains but nothing corrects.
measured_by: grep for DOCTOR-DOWN-EXIT-4 across apps, tests and the receipt directory
the 89-id set from my own clean runs
problems.would_resolve_it: rewrite the comment to describe what the card did (4 was renumbered to 1, correction registered in doctor_exit_code_correction.json, row W0503-DOCTOR-DOWN-EXIT-1), since the comment is the only remaining text claiming 4 is the shipped behaviour.

problems.what: one command_id per process is reused for every step, and the published protocol binds command_id to a content hash. apps/cli/cli_verbs.go:214 mints 'cmd-<verb>-<pid>' once per process; I captured both of interactive's session.send envelopes carrying the same command_id with different text, and the authority's gate keys on (principal, project, v2:method, command_id) at internal/domain/client_protocol.go:687-693, where a differing hash is the hard error IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and an identical hash silently replays the first answer. PIDs are recycled, so two separate goal commands days apart can also collide. I could not reproduce this end-to-end: in my isolated host every method was refused with FORBIDDEN before the idempotency gate, so the recorded rows never accumulated. This is a code-and-envelope finding, not a demonstrated failure, and it is filed as a reservation for that reason.
measured_by: reviewer_captured_envelopes_round2.json (session.list, session.create, session.send, session.send all with command_id cmd-interactive-<pid>)
problems.would_resolve_it: mint a distinct command_id per step (verb, pid and a step counter or the payload digest) and add a row that drives interactive with two stdin messages and requires two different command_id values on the wire; settle the end-to-end question with a host whose project/session preconditions are satisfied, which is what A04 will have.

problems.what: the deliverable 'every command product.contract lists' is still graded against a hand copy rather than the contract. contracts/product.contract.json is not in the repository at all (git ls-files finds no product.contract match and spec/v2.0/contracts holds five other files), so no row can read it; the substitute want-list at tests/runtime/cli_contract/main.go:163-164 is unchanged and still repeats 'init' twice while omitting doctor, interactive, version, help, task and worker, and the '>= 15' help floor round 1 called unfailable is still present alongside the new set-comparison row.
problems.would_resolve_it: either mirror the product contract into the repository under a card that owns spec/ or contracts/ and compare the table against the file, or state plainly in registered_selector_boundary terms that the contract surface is transcribed, drop the duplicate init, and add the six missing names to the want-list.

problems.what: several of the protocol client's local precondition mirrors are unexercised from either side, so they are unverified text rather than tested behaviour: the command_id pattern (R2-M12) and the EmptyPayload key rule (R2-M13b) can be deleted with all 89 green. cli_v2.go is honest about being a deliberate second copy and W0503-CLI-METHOD-TABLE-MATCHES-THE-FROZEN-SCHEMA does compare the 23 names, payload and result type names and sorted required lists against internal/api/contracts/client.protocol.schema.json - but that row compares names, not the write/CAS rules, which is where the blocker lives.
measured_by: R2-M12, R2-M13 and the well-formed R2-M13b in mutation_selfcheck_verifier_round2.json
problems.would_resolve_it: extend the schema row to compare v2WriteMethods against the published method contracts (which methods carry project_id/expected_revision/writer_epoch) and add a probe that makes the CLI send a shape each mirror refuses, so the local rules are exercised rather than transcribed.

problems.what: the two disclosed limits P-R1-7 and P-R1-8 remain open and I reproduced both breaks (R2-M8, R-R2-M9). I am recording them as limitations rather than blockers because remediation_round1.json labels them DISCLOSED_LIMIT with the residual spelled out, files an obligation for each, and makes no claim that is contradicted; the install leg is carried independently by the check's own launch.
problems.would_resolve_it: package-wide os/exec rule with an exemption list naming the accepted coding_task.go, and a candidate that publishes the built binary's digest for the check to compare with the file it launches (the digest is already recorded, only the comparison is missing).

problems.what: the card's evidence set is internally layered in a way a later reader can misread. construction_check_runs.json still reports '3 consecutive runs returned PASS with the same 46 assertion ids' and registered_selector_boundary.json points at it as the executor evidence, while the program now emits 89; only construction_check_final_run.txt carries one 89 run, construction_check_final_run3.txt is a 46 run, and the four-run claim is otherwise supported by the round-5 and round-7 baselines. All 24 digests still match, so nothing is falsified, but the multi-run record for the current program is not on disk.
measured_by: the three files read in this review
my own runs: 8 clean 89-id runs across two HEADs
problems.would_resolve_it: append a new runs file (not editing the hashed one) with the four or five 89-id runs and their report-line digests, and note in it which superseded 46-id artefacts remain for provenance.

own_mutants.overlap_with_prior_rounds: none; the executor ran 14 in round 5 and 5 in round 7 and round 1's reviewer ran 10, and every mutant here attacks a different property with a different anchor
survivors: R2-M3-host-configure-carries-the-epoch (P-R2-1, the blocker: the fix is invisible to the check)
own_mutants.restoration: all 14 restored with git checkout -- <exact path>; restored_clean and restored_sha_matches_baseline true for each; the tree is clean for apps/cli, tests/runtime and ops

survivor_reasons: see the survivor_reasons block of mutation_selfcheck_verifier_round2.json; in one sentence: the check grades what its fixture answers, and the fixture answers a method name rather than validating an envelope, so anything that lives below the method name - the CAS fields, the two statuses it never emits, the status session leg it never requests, the table's method column and the mirrors it never exercises - is unasserted.
limitations: The model-switch blocker is proven at two authorities (the domain decoder replayed with the CLI's own bytes, and a live apps/control process) but not in a host that has the project and session the switch would act on; my isolated data root had no such project, so I measured the refusal rather than a successful switch after the fix.

The idempotency/command_id finding (P-R2-10) is a code-and-envelope reading, not a demonstrated failure: in my run every method was refused with FORBIDDEN before the idempotency gate, so I never observed IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. I have stated that in the problem entry.

I did not run the accepted-cascade shape with no prompt (looksLikeAcceptedRun's default) because it would create a Job Object and spawn a worker in a working tree W13-02 is actively committing to; the measurement is named in judgement_on_run_delegation instead.

The harness is shared: W13-02 landed four commits (ba617cf0, 06b2cd84, 7883e368 and earlier b007e0b9) while I worked, and one of them owns a file this card's check reads. My review did not modify, revert or stage any of them; git status --porcelain for tracked files is empty.

Mutants attack this card's delivered source and its own check program. I did not attack the accepted tests/runtime/check, and I did not reconstruct the executor's intermediate states; the regression history was verified from the invocation receipts on disk (46a887be 7 red rows, c17aec69/4940613b/9628355e PASS 33) plus my own byte-identical re-run.

14 mutants is not a branch survey. Not probed: the config write-failure branches, outJSON's marshal failure, the distribution candidate's non-Windows skip path, the interrupt window other than CTRL_BREAK, and every flag-parse failure inside the accepted verbs.
A04 and A15 were not exercised; no formal case, no parent W05, no W05-99 gate was evaluated or accepted.

Reviewer footprint: working scratch (built binaries, my isolated host data root, probe logs, the drivers before copying) lives under .local/r2 and is gitignored; the reviewer tools and their outputs that matter were copied into execution/v2.4/receipts/W05/W05-03/. The dispatcher created its usual execution/invocations/<uuid> and execution/receipts/W04/... trees. The untracked cli.exe at the repository root predates this review and was left alone.

Concurrent writes by others during this review, none of them mine: git HEAD moved from 41f3cb96 (where this card is parked) through b007e0b9, ba617cf0, 06b2cd84 to 7883e368, all W13-02; apps/desktop/main/lib/v2.js went from untracked to committed at f85fcc8d to 5745e2c5, which is the file W0503-CLI-TABLE-AND-DESKTOP-V2-AGREE reads and why the digest in remediation_round1.json no longer matches (P-R2-7); and execution/v2.4/commands.json gained a test.ui.recovery binding at 10:51 UTC by another agent, which does not touch this card's selectors and postdates my five dispatcher runs. This review wrote nothing outside execution/v2.4/receipts/W05/W05-03/ and .local/, modified or staged no tracked file, and the 24 registered evidence digests still all match at the end.
verdict_scope: REJECT is directed at one measured fact and its two claim sentences, not at the whole increment. What I am NOT rejecting: the verbs now send the contract's operations with the caller's ids and turn every host refusal into a non-zero exit (P-R1-1 is resolved and I re-measured it against the real core); the split settled gate and the write-only-after-the-host-accepts order (P-R1-2's gate half); the doctor exit-code correction, its discovery-path fix and its now-real probes (P-R1-9); resume's epoch on the wire (P-R1-10); the delivered interactive entry and the contract syntaxes (P-R1-5's main half, P-R1-11); the proven_by closure against the attacks it was built for (P-R1-3); the run delegation, which I judge acceptable because the accepted W05-02 report is byte-identical through it; the distribution candidate; the two disclosed limits, which I confirmed rather than contradicted; the registered-selector boundary (P-R1-12); the 24/24 digests; and the scope discipline. A round-3 pass should expect to touch apps/cli/cli_v2.go's host.configure envelope, one assertion in tests/runtime/cli_contract/v2verbs.go (or make the probe decode), the two sentences named in P-R2-1, and then re-measure W05-01, W05-02 and W05-G01 again. Nothing in this verdict says the card is further from acceptance than round 1 left it: it is much closer, and this is the one place where the claim still outruns the measurement.
